title: The Final Simulation
objective: Combine classes, an array of objects, and a while loop into a complete turn-by-turn production simulation.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge capstone combining classes, arrays, and loops into a console-based simulation. All prose and code are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: This is the capstone: bringing together classes, an array of objects, and a while loop into one running simulation. The order queue is just an array of Order instances, and each pass through the loop is one order the worker attempts.

The pattern is: while the worker still has orders waiting and isn't exhausted, look at the next order without removing it yet. If the worker doesn't have enough energy to afford it, the worker collapses right there — log that and stop, leaving that order (and any after it) still in the array. Otherwise, remove the order from the front of the array with .shift(), complete it, and report the worker's remaining energy.

The loop naturally ends one of two ways: the order array becomes empty (orders.length === 0, so the while condition stops being true) or the worker collapses partway through. Checking which one happened after the loop tells you whether to print a success message or a collapse message.
explanation.rule: A simulation loop keeps running while its stop conditions are all still false — check both 'are there orders left?' and 'can the worker still work?' in the same while condition.

examples.title: A Full Run That Succeeds
examples.note: Bo starts with plenty of energy for all three orders (5+5+5=15 <= 20), so the loop empties the array completely and the success branch runs.

checks.question: After runProduction finishes, orders.length is 2 (out of an original 3). What does that tell you?
options: The worker collapsed before finishing the second order.
The worker still has full energy.

feedback.correct: Correct — one order was shifted off (completed) before the worker ran out of energy on the next one, leaving 2 still in the array.
feedback.incorrect: orders.length only shrinks when an order is actually completed and shifted off — leftover orders mean the worker collapsed before reaching them.

assignment.title: Run the Foundry
assignment.brief: Complete runProduction(worker, orders) so it simulates Widget Foundry turn by turn until the orders run out or the worker collapses.
requirements: Define runProduction(worker, orders) using a while loop.
Each pass: if the worker can't afford the next order's effort, log a collapse message, set energy to 0, and stop.
Otherwise remove the order from the front of the array, complete it, and log its completion with the worker's remaining energy.
After the loop, log a success message if all orders were completed, or a collapse message reporting how many orders are still waiting.
assignment.expectedOutput:
Order 1 completed. Energy remaining: 7.
Order 2 completed. Energy remaining: 3.
Rin collapsed before completing Order 3.
Rin collapsed with 1 order(s) still waiting.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: runProduction with Rin(10 energy) against orders [3,4,5] completes 2 orders then collapses on the third

hints: The while condition needs both checks: orders.length > 0 && !worker.isExhausted().
Look at orders[0] first (don't remove it yet) to check whether the worker can afford it.
Only call orders.shift() once you know the worker has enough energy for that order.
For Rin starting at 10 energy against orders costing 3, 4, then 5: 10-3=7, 7-4=3, then 3 is less than 5, so Rin collapses on Order 3 with 1 order left in the array.
